channel.title: AI Tool Lab - AI News
channel.description: Daily AI news briefs with editorial analysis.

item.title: OpenAI countersues Apple over trade secret theft and supplier coercion
item.description: OpenAI filed a countersuit in a California court on Friday, accusing Apple of stealing trade secrets and coercing shared suppliers. The complaint says a former OpenAI employee brought product plans to Apple after returning there. Apple sued OpenAI in summer over alleged employee poaching. OpenAI closed its $6.4 billion acquisition of Jony Ive's io studio and is building its own devices.

item.title: Banned Nvidia Blackwell chips found in Shanghai data center, Bloomberg reports
item.description: Two Chinese companies installed Nvidia Blackwell chips at a Shanghai data center linked to Alice Huang, Bloomberg reports, citing regulatory filings. Shanghai Shuoyao pledged a GB300-NVL72 rack as collateral for a 96 million yuan ($14 million) loan; Shanghai Kezhan listed a GB200 server at the same site. Bloomberg traced the rack to Gigabyte through a serial number in a warranty database. Exporting the chips without a US license is banned.

item.title: nexos.ai platform routes 200+ models through one governed AI gateway
item.description: nexos.ai says its AI Adoption Platform routes requests for more than 200 models through a single gateway that applies per-team budgets, access rules and audit logs. Smart Router selects models by cost, quality and latency; caching and context compression reduce token spend. The company cites SOC 2 Type 2, ISO 27001 and ISO 42001 certification, GDPR compliance, European hosting and zero data retention.

item.title: Tencent open-sources DFly2 drafter that reuses the target model's sparse KV cache
item.description: Tencent open-sourced DFly2, a 0.85-billion-parameter, five-layer drafter for sparse-attention models. Each draft layer reuses the target's KV cache and top-k indexer picks, adding no draft KV memory. Serving tests on DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash at 64K context show up to 81% higher throughput at matched per-user speed; greedy decoding speedup reaches 2.97x on H20 GPUs.

item.title: OpenAI says heavy ChatGPT users may hit limits sooner as it merges Chat and Work
item.description: OpenAI began rolling out a unified Chat and Work experience in ChatGPT to a small group of Pro subscribers, Thibault Sottiaux said. The two surfaces share one usage meter; OpenAI says most users should not see more frequent resets, though a small fraction of heavy users may hit limits sooner. Instant-model conversations stay unlimited and do not count toward the shared allowance, which OpenAI plans to extend in December.

item.title: Sakana AI releases Namazu Small 30B reasoning model built on Nemotron 3 Nano
item.description: Sakana AI built Namazu Small, a 30B-A3B reasoning model, on NVIDIA's Nemotron 3 Nano pretrained base using its own continued pretraining and post-training. Across 25 benchmarks it averages 60.1, beating the 120B Nemotron 3 Super at 56.2 and the Nano baseline at 50.2. BrowseComp reaches 73.5 versus 36.1, while SimpleQA Verified falls to 6.8.

item.title: Nvidia pauses server shipments to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia
item.description: Citing a Wall Street Journal report, Nvidia told manufacturing partners including Dell and Super Micro to pause server shipments to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia for an unspecified period while it checks compliance with U.S. export rules. Those markets became a route for remote access to Nvidia chips from China; the Institute for Progress estimates such data centers supply about 24% of China's AI computing power.

item.title: Scott Aaronson says AI math proofs matter more than the Riemann result
item.description: Scott Aaronson, a complexity theorist and former OpenAI researcher, argues that AI's math breakthroughs matter less for their results than for the capability they demonstrate. He highlights OpenAI proofs that add matching lower bounds to faster matrix multiplication and Fourier transform algorithms, showing where speedups stop. He says he now believes a proof of P ≠ NP is near and claims AI labs hold undisclosed cryptography bombshells.

item.title: OpenAI patches billing bug that changed GPT-6.2 usage limits
item.description: A billing bug during the GPT-6.2 rollout gave subscribers incorrect discounts, OpenAI Codex engineer Thibault Sottiaux said. After the fix, Astra users reach usage limits 40% faster and Sol users 25% faster than last week, though quotas still last longer than on GPT-6. Go, Plus, Pro and Business subscribers get an extra saved reset; Business users also receive free Fast Mode through year-end, with no retroactive charges.

item.title: Grand Theft Auto VI sold $3.79B on day one without generative AI
item.description: Grand Theft Auto VI earned $3.79 billion in day-one retail sales and became the highest-rated game on Metacritic after a 13-year wait, according to TechCrunch. Rockstar built it without generative AI, with about 5,000 people working for more than a decade and 30,000 distinct nonplayable characters. Its launch coincided with Anthropic's record $81.3 billion IPO.

item.title: 42 state AGs seek to block Character.AI chat sale in bankruptcy
item.description: A bipartisan coalition of 42 state attorneys general is seeking to block Character.AI from auctioning user chat histories during Chapter 11 bankruptcy. The proposed sale covers more than 21 million U.S. accounts, including over 2.1 million registered to minors, with no requirement that a buyer honor existing privacy policies or let users delete data. Character.AI filed for bankruptcy in October.

item.title: TheoPhysEval finds AI agents solve 49 of 50 physics problems
item.description: TheoPhysEval gives AI agents 50 unpublished, research-level theoretical physics problems that a world expert typically needs about a day to solve. GPT-6-Astra running in Codex answered 49 of 50 correctly after a single human prompt, at less than $3 of compute per correct answer. Removing web search and background papers changed accuracy only slightly, which the authors read as evidence of memorized literature.

item.title: OpenAI and Cisco open-source Shirudo for live Linux defense
item.description: OpenAI and Cisco released Shirudo, a BSD-2-Clause eBPF runtime that lets approved AI agents deploy signed, temporary shields on running Linux systems while permanent patches are tested. A Codex-generated guard blocked a Java4Shell exploit against Elasticsearch 9.5.5 without a restart. Shields require a patched bpf-next kernel and TPM 2.0 attestation, and the project remains pre-release.

item.title: S&P puts Nvidia AA rating on negative watch over key-man risk
item.description: S&P Global Ratings placed Nvidia's AA issuer and senior unsecured ratings on negative watch, citing weak executive oversight, no succession plan and reliance on CEO Jensen Huang. The review should conclude within 90 days and could cut the rating to AA-, the fourth-highest grade. Nvidia backstops 25% of a $500 billion AI infrastructure financing package, and a downgrade would likely prompt lenders to demand larger guarantees.

item.title: Google's My Channel patent outlines personalized AI video feeds from user data
item.description: Google's My Channel patent, filed in May and published last week, was rejected but could be refiled. It describes prompts built from viewing history, demographics, IP addresses, GPS data and live news, fed to an LLM on Google servers to generate personalized videos. The filing also covers avatars made from users' own photos, videos and audio, casting them as characters inside the generated content.

item.title: US chip and anti-distillation curbs slow DeepSeek, Moonshot and Alibaba
item.description: The Information reports that since September, curbs on remote access to Nvidia chips abroad and stronger anti-distillation defenses from OpenAI and Anthropic have delayed Chinese AI projects. DeepSeek researchers estimate their gap to top US models could widen from three to six months to nine. Moonshot AI canceled a $150 million Blackwell chip deal in Indonesia, while MiniMax, MiHoYo and Alibaba lean more heavily on domestic silicon.

item.title: RUSI researcher details why militaries target cloud data centers
item.description: RUSI researcher Joseph Jarnecki told an Ars Live discussion that cloud sites running battlefield management, HR and resource management can become military objectives under international law. He cited this year's strikes on Amazon facilities in the Gulf and Russia-Ukraine drone exchanges, putting Gulf data-center investment at over 100 times Iranian drone cost. Ukraine moved government data abroad after the 2022 invasion.

item.title: AI-drafted requests and data brokers strain US public records offices
item.description: US public records offices face a surge from data brokers and chatbot-written requests. Federal agencies received a record 1.7 million FOIA requests last year; one analysis found at least 29% of Education Department requests in July were partly AI-written, twice as long, with 83% demanding long lists. Startups have raised over $100 million to turn filings into sales signals, while Pennsylvania appeals are projected at 6,000 this year.

item.title: HKU and ByteDance Seed open-source Laminar async RL post-training framework
item.description: HKU and ByteDance Seed released Laminar, an Apache-2.0 framework that decouples rollout, buffering, training and weight sync for agent RL. On SWE-bench Verified, Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B rose from 46.6% to 52.2%; matching the baseline's 51.4% took 46% fewer samples and 71% fewer GPU-hours. Tests scaled to 1,024 H800 GPUs.

item.title: DeepMind pairs Gemini with mass spectrometry tools in Antigravity skills
item.description: DeepMind's Mass Spec Skills let Antigravity agents chain formula search, PubChem lookups and fragment checks to identify molecules from tandem mass spectra. On 100 catalogued compounds, Gemini 3.8 Flash, Gemini 4 Argon and Gemini 4 Carbon reached about 97% exact identification with the skills, versus under 4% offline; token use fell nearly fourfold on Flash. Spectral libraries alone annotate only about 5% of measured spectra.

item.title: Amateur astronomers use Codex and Astra to flag exoplanet candidates
item.description: OpenAI engineer Kevin Bond used Codex to search about 100,000 Kepler stars, flagging over 200 signals including 10 known planets; a SETI Institute astronomer independently found the same two candidates, one a dip every 13.8 days. Separately, Ethan Byrd used Astra on data from roughly 19 million stars and produced 49 candidates, sending his strongest to NASA's TESS team for analysis.

item.title: Meta details LLM pipeline behind Facebook Your Algorithm ranking
item.description: Meta detailed the engineering behind Your Algorithm, which lets Facebook users type interests for Feed and Reels. Each typed interest drives four retrieval sources, and a fine-tuned LLM reranker outputs only items to remove, which Meta says beat a general-purpose model on speed and reliability. The system passed no user metrics.

item.title: Anthropic lets users install Claude Artifacts as macOS and Windows apps
item.description: Anthropic began beta-testing installation of Claude Artifacts as macOS and Windows apps, requiring the latest Claude desktop client. Installed apps can call OS APIs, connectors and Claude itself to add menu bar items, transparent windows and notifications. A free account is enough, and Apple Developer accounts can build standalone apps.

item.title: Jensen Huang apologizes to Nvidia staff, denies Trump helped reinstate him
item.description: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang apologized to staff in his first all-hands since returning, calling claims that Trump directly secured his reinstatement completely untrue. He said politics played no role and acknowledged violating the company's code of conduct, adding that he is in therapy daily. Huang resigned on November 12 and was reinstated Monday.

item.title: AI agents generate 450% more network traffic than human workers
item.description: A report sponsored by Tata Communications says tasks run by AI agents generate an estimated 450 percent more network traffic than the same tasks done by people. As inference moves on-premises for lower latency, as few as half of enterprises believe their networks can handle AI's bandwidth demands. The report points to network-as-a-service and AI observability as responses.

item.title: GPT-6 models design proteins using reasoning and code, study reports
item.description: OpenAI reported that GPT-6 models can design protein structures and sequences using reasoning and code, without specialized biology models. In wet-lab tests, 35 of 322 designed minibinders bound across five targets, a 10.9 percent hit rate. On MotifBench the models scored 43.7 percent versus 27.8 percent for specialized approaches.

item.title: DeepMind agent teams cut quantum algorithm costs using Lean proofs
item.description: DeepMind used teams of Gemini 4 agents to optimize quantum algorithms, proving each circuit correct with the Lean theorem prover and open-sourcing the library. For inertial confinement fusion, agents cut computing cost 11.8-fold and memory from 5,650 to 4,338 error-corrected qubits. They also found a 290-fold speedup for arcsin and 2.5-fold for Cytochrome P450 simulations.

item.title: Honeypot Research Exposes Data-Theft Chain Among AI Inference Providers
item.description: Dragos' 2 million honeypot requests found at least 3 providers compromised and hundreds of AWS keys stolen and used; OpenRouter removed 3 and revoked ZDR eligibility for 125 endpoints.

item.title: Riemann Hypothesis Proof Formally Certified by Lean Community
item.description: The Lean and Mathlib communities issued a statement confirming that mathematician Alpöge’s proof of the Riemann Hypothesis has passed verification: about 17 million lines of code, dozens of people independently reproduced consistent results, and certification was obtained within 24 hours.

item.title: AA Evaluation: GPT-6.2 More Concise but Less Transparent
item.description: AA personality benchmark: both GPT-6.2 models give answers 34–40% shorter, admitting uncertainty falls to 24 and 51, and transparency at 41 and 57 trails Claude's 81 and 90.
